rationale: Both candidates surface the ground-truth themes (regression tests already added, CuMemTag enum underused/half-utilized), so recall is similar and modest since the human thread was thin and already resolved. Y is more precise and actionable: it finds a genuine bug the diff introduces (sleep(level=1) after a prior level=2 never clears _level2_sleeping, permanently blocking wake_up), flags a stale mock (_is_sleeping) left over from the removed attribute, and — critically — explicitly identifies that existing tests calling sleep(level=2)+wake_up() will now crash under the new NotImplementedError guard, directly hitting the latent gap about the guard being too strict for existing callers. X is thorough and well-organized (good default-level=2 footgun catch) but stays at the design-tradeoff level rather than pinpointing concrete broken call sites, and doesn't connect its concerns to existing tests/CI exercising the guarded path, so it misses the gap.
